title: Projects
text:
Comparing Classical Methods, SVMs, CNN-BiLSTM, and ESM-2 Embeddings
Objective: To build an end-to-end protein sequence modelling pipeline for eukaryotic signal-peptide prediction, benchmarking classical and deep learning approaches against modern protein language model embeddings.
Approach:

Data Preparation

Used high-confidence UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot annotations.
Applied MMseqs2 clustering for redundancy reduction and biologically meaningful train/benchmark splits.

Model Comparison

Benchmarked the classical von Heijne PSWM, a biochemical-feature SVM, a CNN-BiLSTM, and an ESM-2 embedding-based model.

Evaluation & Interpretation

Achieved F1 = 0.962 and MCC = 0.957 on a held-out benchmark using the ESM-2-based model.
Analyzed amino-acid composition, signal-peptide lengths, kingdom-specific bias, and cleavage-site motifs.


Tech Stack: Python, PyTorch, ESM-2, MMseqs2, scikit-learn

Key Insight: Protein language model embeddings substantially outperformed classical statistical and hand-engineered feature approaches, underscoring the value of learned representations for functional prediction tasks.

GitHub Repository




Profile HMMs vs. Sequence-Similarity Search
Objective: To build an automated protein domain annotation workflow connecting classical homology detection with modern representation-learning approaches, comparing sequence-based and structure-informed HMM profiling for Kunitz/BPTI-type domain detection.
Approach:

Alignment & Profiling

Processed protein structure-derived alignments to support domain-level annotation.

Classification

Compared profile-based (HMMER) and sequence-similarity-based (MMseqs2) classification workflows, with 2-fold cross-validation.

Evaluation

Achieved MCC = 0.997 (profile-HMM) and MCC = 0.991 (sequence-similarity).


Tech Stack: HMMER, MMseqs2, Python, Bash

Key Insight: Profile-HMM approaches slightly outperformed sequence-similarity search, reinforcing their value for remote homology detection and protein family classification.

GitHub Repository




R/Bioconductor Workflow for Array-Based Methylation Data
Objective: To identify differentially methylated regions and epigenetic signatures between healthy and diseased individuals using Illumina 450K array data.
Approach:

QC & Normalization using minfi.
Exploratory Analysis — PCA for batch-effect assessment, heatmaps of variable CpG sites.
Differential Methylation — identified DMRs, visualized with volcano plots.

Tech Stack: R, Bioconductor, minfi

Key Insight: PCA-based batch-effect assessment confirmed biological group as the dominant source of variance, validating the experimental design.

GitHub Repository

title: Projects
text:
Deep Learning & Medical Imaging

Chest X-Ray Pneumonia Detection via Transfer Learning
ResNet50 vs. EfficientNetB0 vs. DenseNet-121 XRV
Objective: To compare transfer-learning architectures for pneumonia classification under class imbalance, with a focus on clinically relevant evaluation.
Approach:

Model Comparison — ResNet50, EfficientNetB0, DenseNet-121 XRV.
Imbalance & Thresholding — addressed class imbalance, evaluated threshold-selection strategies using clinically relevant metrics.
Interpretability — applied ensembling, test-time augmentation, and Grad-CAM.

Tech Stack: PyTorch, TensorFlow, Grad-CAM

Key Insight: DenseNet-121 XRV achieved the strongest performance under the maximum-MCC threshold strategy.
